mainTopic: רבי's view on the קנס and the word 'לבדו', how רבי יוחנן learns two laws from 'בעולת בעל', when קידושי ביאה takes effect, and whether ביאה creates נשואין or אירוסין
overview: On the previous daf, רבי and the רבנן argued about several men who were with a נערה המאורסה in an unusual way. רבי זירא says that even רבי agrees all the men pay the קנס. The death penalty is different only because the פסוק says 'לבדו'. The רבנן use 'לבדו' for another lesson: the man can be put to death alone, as רבי יונתן teaches. Next, the גמרא shows how רבי יוחנן learns two laws from the words 'בעולת בעל'. The גמרא then asks whether קידושי ביאה takes effect at the start or at the end of the act. אמימר in the name of רבא answers that it takes effect at the end, because that is what the man has in mind. Last, the גמרא asks whether ביאה creates נשואין or only אירוסין. אביי's proof from a משנה is pushed aside, and רבא begins a new proof from a ברייתא about a girl three years and one day old, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי זירא: רבי agrees that everyone pays the fine
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא limits רבי's view: for the קנס, every one of the men pays.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: רבי agrees that, for the fine, all of them pay.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא says that even רבי, who treated only the first man as sinning with a 'virgin' for the death penalty, agrees that all the men pay the קנס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the death penalty, רבי treats the girl as no longer a בתולה after the first man. For the קנס, though, רבי זירא says every man pays as if she were still a בתולה. This sets up an obvious question: why treat her differently for the two laws?

keyTerms.meaning: agrees (here: even רבי agrees)
a fixed fine set by the Torah (here the payment for violating or seducing a בתולה)
they pay

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
Rabbi concedes regarding the fine
phrases.notes: 'רבי' with no name means רבי יהודה הנשיא. The fine is the money paid for violating or seducing a בתולה.

phrases.english: that they all pay.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: מוֹדֶה רַבִּי לְעִנְיַן קְנָס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רבי's view from the earlier argument on the daf to the death penalty only.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even according to רבי, every man pays the קנס.

steps.title: Why is the fine different from the death penalty?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the קנס should be treated differently from the death penalty.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between this and the death penalty?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי זירא: if for the death penalty only the first man counts as being with a בתולה, why should all the men pay the קנס?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question looks inconsistent. Either she is still a בתולה after the first man or she is not. If she is, all should get סקילה. If she isn't, the later men should not pay the קנס.

keyTerms.meaning: what is different? (asking for a reason to split two cases)
killing; the death penalty

phrases.english: What is different from the death penalty?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the consistency of רבי זירא's statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's claim that רבי agrees all pay the קנס.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי treats her as no longer a בתולה for the death penalty, so he should do the same for the קנס.

steps.title: The death penalty is different because of the word 'only'
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק says 'the man who lay with her shall die alone', so only one man gets the virgin's death penalty.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because the פסוק says: 'Then the man who lay with her shall die, alone.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a special word in the פסוק, 'לבדו', limits the death penalty to one man. The קנס has no such limiting word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי's split does not come from logic about her status. It comes from a פסוק. 'לבדו' teaches that only one man gets the סקילה of a נערה המאורסה בתולה. Since no such word appears for the קנס, all the men pay.

keyTerms.meaning: it is different there
because the פסוק says
alone; only him

phrases.english: It is different there,
since the verse says:
"Then the man who lay with her shall die, alone."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by pointing to a special פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Scriptural limitation: a word in the פסוק applies only to the death penalty.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Her status should be the same for both laws.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word 'לבדו' limits only the death penalty to one man. The קנס stays the same for all.

steps.title: What do the רבנן do with the word 'לבדו'?
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן say all the men get סקילה, so what do they learn from 'לבדו'?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, what do they do with this word 'alone'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the רבנן, who give all the men סקילה, explain the word 'לבדו'. Every word in the Torah must teach something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'לבדו' means only one man gets סקילה, the רבנן seem to ignore it. So they must use the word for some other lesson. The next step tells us what it is.

keyTerms.meaning: the Sages (the majority view arguing with רבי)
what do they do with it? (how do they use this word)

phrases.english: And the Rabbis, this "alone"
what do they do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן הַאי לְבַדּוֹ מַאי עָבְדִי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from רבי's use of the פסוק to the other side of the argument.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson the רבנן learn from 'לבדו'.

steps.title: The רבנן use 'לבדו' for רבי יונתן's teaching
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבי אושעיא says both must be punishable for either to die. רבי יונתן uses 'לבדו' to show the man can die alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: They need it for what a ברייתא teaches: 'Then they shall both die' means not unless both are equal, says רבי אושעיא. רבי יונתן says: 'Then the man who lay with her shall die, alone.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the רבנן use 'לבדו' for a different lesson, taught in a ברייתא where רבי אושעיא and רבי יונתן argue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אושעיא reads 'both of them shall die' to mean that if one of them can't be punished, the other isn't punished either. רבי יונתן answers with 'לבדו': sometimes only the man dies. So the רבנן use 'לבדו' for this, and not to limit the death penalty to the first man.

keyTerms.meaning: they need it (for another lesson)
like what was taught in a ברייתא
equal as one; both in the same legal state

phrases.english: They need it for what was taught in a ברייתא:
"Then they shall both of them die" —
not unless the two are equal as one,
these are the words of Rabbi Oshaya.
Rabbi Yonatan says:
"Then the man who lay with her shall die, alone."
phrases.notes: He means the man can be put to death by himself, even when she is not punished.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers what the רבנן learn from 'לבדו'.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן use 'לבדו' like רבי יונתן: the man can be executed even when the woman is not punishable.
steps.whatToRemember: 'לבדו' teaches רבי that only the first man gets סקילה. The רבנן use the same word for רבי יונתן's lesson that the man may die alone. The קנס, according to everyone, is paid by all the men.

steps.title: Where does רבי יוחנן get the other rule?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן uses 'בעולת בעל' for קידושי ביאה. So where does he learn that only a husband makes her a בעולה through unusual relations?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן, where does he get this idea from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about רבי יוחנן. He used the words 'בעולת בעל' to prove that ביאה can make קידושין. So where does he learn the other rule, that only her husband makes her a 'בעולה' through unusual relations?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier on the daf, 'בעולת בעל' was used for the idea that only the husband makes her a בעולה שלא כדרכה. But רבי יוחנן already used those same words as the source for קידושי ביאה. It seems one phrase can't teach both laws.

keyTerms.meaning: an idea or line of reasoning
from where does he know it?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan,
this idea, from where does he get it?
phrases.notes: 'This idea' is the rule that only her husband makes her count as a בעולה through unusual relations.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, הַאי סְבָרָא מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the רבנן's use of 'לבדו' to a similar question about רבי יוחנן's use of 'בעולת בעל'.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source רבי יוחנן uses for the rule that only the husband makes her a בעולה שלא כדרכה.

steps.title: 'בעולת בעל' teaches two laws
steps.stepSummary: The Torah could have written 'בעולת איש'. Writing 'בעולת בעל' instead lets us learn two laws.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the פסוק write 'בעולת איש'. Why does it say 'בעולת בעל'? Learn two things from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the unusual wording 'בעל' instead of 'איש' is extra. That extra gives room to learn both laws from the same phrase.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plain phrase would teach only one law. The Torah picked a special word, 'בעל' (husband), instead of the simple 'איש' (man). That extra shows the phrase carries two lessons: ביאה can make קידושין, and only the husband makes her a בעולה שלא כדרכה.

keyTerms.meaning: if so
a woman who had relations with a man
a woman who had relations with a husband
learn two things from it

phrases.english: If so, let the verse write "be'ulat ish",
what is "be'ulat ba'al"? —
Learn two things from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן נִכְתּוֹב קְרָא בְּעוּלַת אִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about רבי יוחנן's source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra wording in the פסוק lets one phrase teach two laws.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One phrase can only teach one law.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the Torah said 'בעל' and not 'איש', the phrase teaches both קידושי ביאה and that only the husband makes her a בעולה שלא כדרכה.
steps.whatToRemember: Unusual wording in a פסוק can let one phrase teach more than one law. Here 'בעולת בעל' teaches two.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוחנן learns both laws from 'בעולת בעל'. The Torah could have written 'בעולת איש', so the word 'בעל' teaches both קידושי ביאה and that only the husband makes her a בעולה שלא כדרכה.

steps.title: Does betrothal by relations take effect at the start or the end?
steps.stepSummary: New question: does קידושי ביאה take effect at the start or at the end of the act? The practical case: another man gives her קידושין in the middle.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: does the beginning of ביאה acquire, or the end? The difference: where he began relations with her, and she reached out her hand and accepted קידושין from another man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about קידושי ביאה: at what moment do the קידושין take effect? It also gives a case where the answer would matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ביאה is not a single instant. If the beginning acquires, the first man's קידושין already took effect, and the second man's קידושין mean nothing. If only the end acquires, the second man's קידושין came first and she is engaged to him.

keyTerms.meaning: a question was asked among them (an open question)
the beginning of the act of relations
the end of the act of relations
the practical difference that comes out of it
began relations (the first stage)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the case is about two men both having relations with her. The second man gives קידושין the usual way (like money), into her hand, while the first man's ביאה is still going on.

phrases.english: A question was asked of them:
Does the beginning of intercourse acquire
or does the end of intercourse acquire?
The practical difference comes out
in a case where he began relations with her,
and she reached out her hand
and accepted betrothal from another man.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: תְּחִילַּת בִּיאָה קוֹנָה אוֹ סוֹף בִּיאָה קוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about the exact moment קידושי ביאה takes effect.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether קידושי ביאה takes effect at the start or at the end of the act, shown through a case where another man gives her קידושין in the middle.
steps.whyThisMatters: It decides which of two men she is engaged to, and so which man's קידושין count.

steps.title: A second practical difference: a כהן גדול marrying a בתולה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives another case where it matters whether קידושי ביאה works at the start or the end of the act: a כהן גדול who betroths a בתולה through ביאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Alternatively, the question matters for a כהן גדול who acquires a בתולה through ביאה. What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still asking the question from Step 8. Now it offers a second case where the answer makes a real difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן גדול may only marry a בתולה. If קידושין takes effect only at the end of the act, she is no longer a בתולה at that moment. Then a כהן גדול could never betroth through ביאה. If it takes effect at the start, he could.

keyTerms.meaning: Alternatively; or also
The High Priest
A virgin

phrases.english: Alternatively, for a High Priest
who acquires a virgin through intercourse,
phrases.notes: A כהן גדול may marry only a בתולה (ויקרא 21:14). If the קידושין happens at the end of the act, she is no longer one at that moment.

phrases.english: what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי, לְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל דְּקָא קָנֵי בְּתוּלָה בְּבִיאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second practical case to the question raised in Step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does קידושי ביאה take effect at the start or the end of the act, as shown by the case of a כהן גדול and a בתולה?

steps.title: A man intends the act to count at its completion
steps.stepSummary: אמימר in the name of רבא answers that anyone who has relations intends the end of the act, so קידושין takes effect at the end.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said in the name of רבא: Anyone who has intercourse has the completion of intercourse in mind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The קידושין takes effect at the end of the act, because that is what the man has in mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer depends on the man's intention, not on physical details. Since he means the whole completed act to be the קנין, the קידושין happens only at the end. So another man's קידושין in the middle would work, and a כהן גדול would not be able to betroth a בתולה this way.

keyTerms.meaning: One who has intercourse
His intention; what he has in mind
The completion of the act of intercourse

steps.whatToRemember: קידושי ביאה takes effect at the end of the act, because the man's intention is for the completed act.

phrases.english: Ameimar said in the name of Rava:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַבּוֹעֵל – דַּעְתּוֹ עַל גְּמַר בִּיאָה.
phrases.english: Anyone who has intercourse has the completion of intercourse in mind.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַמֵּימָר מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא: כׇּל הַבּוֹעֵל דַּעְתּוֹ עַל גְּמַר בִּיאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Steps 8 and 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: קידושין takes effect at the end of the act, since the man intends the completed act.

steps.title: Does ביאה create engagement or full marriage?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: does קידושי ביאה create נשואין or only אירוסין? The practical differences are inheritance, a כהן becoming טמא for her, and cancelling her vows.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: Does intercourse create marriage, or does it create only betrothal? The practical difference is whether he inherits from her, becomes impure for her, and can cancel her vows. If you say it creates marriage, he inherits from her, becomes impure for her, and cancels her vows. If you say it creates betrothal, he does not inherit from her, does not become impure for her, and does not cancel her vows. What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a brand-new question about how strong קידושי ביאה is. It then spells out exactly what depends on the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Marriage has two stages: אירוסין, where she is bound to him but not yet living with him, and נשואין, full marriage. Since ביאה is normally part of married life, maybe it brings her straight into נשואין. Three laws depend on this: a husband inherits his wife, a כהן becomes טמא to bury his wife, and a husband alone can cancel his wife's vows. All three apply only after נשואין.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them
Full marriage, the second stage
Betrothal, the first stage of marriage
The practical difference
Cancelling vows

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two stages. אֵירוּסִין (also called קידושין) already makes her a married woman in some ways, but rights like inheritance belong only to נִשּׂוּאִין.

phrases.english: A question was asked:

phrases.aramaic: בִּיאָה נִשּׂוּאִין עוֹשָׂה, אוֹ אֵירוּסִין עוֹשָׂה?
phrases.english: Does intercourse create marriage, or does it create betrothal?
The practical difference: to inherit from her,
and to become impure for her, and to cancel her vows.
phrases.notes: "Impure for her" means a כהן becoming טמא to bury her, which he does for his wife.

phrases.english: If you say it creates marriage,
he inherits from her, becomes impure for her, and cancels her vows;
and if you say it creates betrothal,
he does not inherit from her and does not become impure for her
and does not cancel her vows.
phrases.notes: He means he can't cancel them on his own. During אירוסין, the father takes part too.

phrases.english: What is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: בִּיאָה נִשּׂוּאִין עוֹשָׂה, אוֹ אֵירוּסִין עוֹשָׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about קידושי ביאה, separate from the timing question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does קידושי ביאה bring her into נשואין, or only אירוסין?

steps.title: אביי brings a משנה about a father's rights over his daughter
steps.stepSummary: אביי begins a proof from a משנה. It lists a father's rights over his daughter, including her קידושין through ביאה, and then says what more a husband gets once she is married.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Come and hear: A father has rights over his daughter in her betrothal, whether by money, document, or intercourse. He has a right to what she finds and to her earnings, and to cancel her vows. He accepts her divorce document, but he does not eat the profits of her property during her lifetime. Once she is married, the husband has more than him, because he eats the profits during her lifetime.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי starts to answer the question by quoting a משנה. This step only sets up the source; the actual proof comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists ביאה as a way the father can betroth his daughter, which belongs to the father's stage of rights. It then separates that stage from "נישאת", when she is married and the husband takes over. אביי will use this split to show whether ביאה counts as אירוסין or נשואין.

keyTerms.meaning: A found object
Her earnings
Eats the profits of her property
A divorce document

phrases.english: Abaye said: Come and hear:
A father has rights over his daughter in her betrothal
by money, by document, and by intercourse,
and he has a right to what she finds and to her earnings,
and to cancel her vows, and he accepts her divorce document,
but he does not eat the profits during her lifetime.
Once she is married, the husband has more than him,
in that he eats the profits during her lifetime.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: תָּא שְׁמַע: הָאָב זַכַּאי בְּבִתּוֹ בְּקִדּוּשֶׁיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of Step 11 with a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: Whether קידושי ביאה creates אירוסין or נשואין
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in כתובות 46b listing a father's rights, including קידושין through ביאה, set apart from the stage of "נישאת"

steps.title: The משנה mentions intercourse first and marriage afterward
steps.stepSummary: אביי finishes his proof. The משנה mentions קידושין through ביאה and only afterward mentions 'she married,' so ביאה seems to create only אירוסין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה teaches 'intercourse,' and then it teaches 'she married'!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי draws the conclusion from the משנה he quoted in the last step. The father's rights include her קידושין through ביאה, and only after that does the משנה talk about her getting married. So ביאה must be only the first stage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ביאה already made her fully married, the משנה would not need a separate, later stage called 'she married.' The order of the משנה suggests ביאה produces only אירוסין, and נשואין comes later. This is the proof's punchline.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches (the משנה or ברייתא says)
She got married (reached the stage of נשואין)
Full marriage, the second stage after אירוסין
Betrothal, the first stage of marriage

phrases.english: It teaches 'intercourse,' and it teaches 'she married'!
phrases.notes: He means the משנה from the last step: first the father's rights over ביאה, and later 'once she married.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof that אביי began in step 12 by stating what the משנה implies.
steps.raayaObject: That קידושי ביאה creates only אירוסין, not נשואין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה listing a father's rights, which mentions ביאה first and 'she married' as a later stage.

steps.title: 'She married' refers to the other ways of betrothal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects אביי's proof. 'She married' refers to קידושין through money or a document, not to ביאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it teaches 'she married,' it is talking about the others.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on אביי's proof. The later line about marriage may refer only to the other ways of making קידושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists three ways a woman can receive קידושין: money, a document, and ביאה. With money or a document, there really is a separate later stage of נשואין. For ביאה, the question stays open, so the משנה proves nothing about it.

keyTerms.meaning: About the others (the other cases in the list)
When it teaches... (opens a reinterpretation)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not say ביאה creates נשואין. It only says this משנה does not prove that it doesn't, so the question is still open.

phrases.english: When it teaches 'she married,' it is about the others.
phrases.notes: 'The others' are money and a document, the two other ways of making קידושין in that משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference drawn in step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects אביי's proof entirely. The question from step 11 stays unresolved.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed 'she married' applies to every method in the list. It may apply only to money and a document.

steps.title: רבא begins a proof about a girl three years and one day old
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a ברייתא: a girl aged three years and one day can receive קידושין through ביאה. A יבם acquires her through ביאה, others are liable for relations with her as an אשת איש, and she can make someone טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Come and hear: A girl of three years and one day can receive קידושין through intercourse. If her יבם has relations with her, he acquires her. One is liable for relations with her because she is a married woman. And she makes the man who has relations with her טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens a new attempt to answer whether ביאה creates נשואין or אירוסין. He starts quoting a ברייתא, and this sets up the next move, because the proof itself comes from how the ברייתא continues.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists laws that apply to a very young girl who received קידושין through ביאה. It treats her seriously as a wife in several ways. רבא will try to show from these details what kind of status ביאה gives her.

keyTerms.meaning: A girl three years and one day old, the youngest age at which ביאה counts halachically
The brother of a man who died childless, who may marry the widow
He acquired her (she becomes his wife)
A married woman; relations with her are a severe sin
The man who has relations with her

phrases.english: Rava said: Come and hear:
A girl three years and one day old
can be betrothed through intercourse,
and if a yavam has relations with her, he acquires her,
and one is liable for her as a married woman,
and she makes the man who has relations with her impure
phrases.notes: This applies if she is a נדה; he becomes טמא just as with an adult woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After אביי's proof was rejected, רבא offers a new proof for the question asked in step 11.
steps.raayaObject: Whether קידושי ביאה creates נשואין or only אירוסין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a girl three years and one day old who receives קידושין through ביאה. The ברייתא continues past this point.
